title: Control plane sell story: ops narrative & competitor scan
content:
Purpose
---
Notes + quick scripts for field to explain Redwood Private control plane to regulated buyers (healthcare, finserv, federal). Includes competitive observations and short rebut lines for common procurement objections. This is a working kit — share feedback and add seat-specific examples.

Audience
- Compliance officers, security/infra architects, procurement leads, platform engineers evaluating private/VPC deployments.

Core one-liner to start a convo
- "Redwood Private puts model serving inside your network perimeter while letting you keep rollout, observability and policy controls in your hands — minimal SaaS metadata and full auditability."

Top-level themes to weave into every conversation
1) Data custody + minimal SaaS footprint — emphasize telemetry governance and optional airgap.
2) Deterministic operational surface — model version pinning, predictable throughput, SLA tiers for dedicated capacity.
3) Verifiable controls for auditors — KMS-integration, configurable audit log retention, evidence bundles for model changes.
4) Graceful availability model — local fallback variants and multi-region routing for continuity.
5) Lower TCO through batching/caching tunables while maintaining latency SLOs.

Short technical summary for architects (elevator)
- Control plane components run in your VPC: deployment manager, policy store, and optional telemetry collector. Management plane endpoints talk over mTLS, no persistent customer data is stored in our hosted control plane unless you opt-in for managed backups. Keys can be customer-managed (KMS/HSM). Audit logs produced are structured, signed, and exportable to SIEMs.

Common buyer objections + suggested rebuttals (concise)
1) "We don't trust any external control plane."
  - Counter: "We provide a private control plane option with the control endpoints hosted in your VPC and an air-gapped on-prem package. For most buyers the hosted control plane can be configured to only hold metadata pointers (no customer content). We also offer a SOC2-ready operational runbook and can include a technical escrow for critical components."
2) "Too risky to surface telemetry off network."
  - Counter: "Telemetry is pluggable: send only anonymized metrics, or run the collector locally and export to your SIEM. We document exactly which fields we collect and provide a sanitized mode for regulated pilots."
3) "Lock-in fears: if we adopt Redwood Private, can we migrate later?"
  - Counter: "Model artifacts, pinned versions, and config are exportable as structured bundles. We support staged migration patterns and provide a handoff checklist for in-house infra teams."
4) "Performance concerns vs single-tenant dedicated providers."
  - Counter: "Our runtime optimizes kernels and KV cache placement for your hardware. We publish per-model performance envelopes and can run a short performance pilot to demonstrate SLOs on your hardware."
5) "Vendor claims about encryption at rest/network are generic. How are you different?"
  - Counter: "We integrate with customer KMS/HSM so keys never leave your control, and we provide signed audit artifacts for config and model rollouts — not just passive logs. That signed trail is the difference auditors ask for."

Competitive scan (high-level, internal shorthand)
- Vendor A (large cloud provider): strong on infra and console familiarity; weaker on ML runtime tuning and token-level cost controls. Likely objections: buyer already on their cloud + concern about double-billing. Our angle: superior inference economics and model-aware optimizations, plus deployment parity across cloud and on-prem.
- Vendor B (inference-only startup): strong runtime; weak on enterprise procurement/sales ops and compliance story. Likely objections: smaller vendor risk. Our angle: combine runtime performance with enterprise sales DNA (contracts, evidence packages, SOC2 + legal templates).
- Vendor C (SaaS-first LLM API): easiest for devs but fails regulated use cases. Our angle: same developer ergonomics with a private control plane option and clear auditors' artifacts.

What buyers actually care about (ranking from interviews)
1) Auditability and evidence for model outputs and change events.
2) Control of encryption keys.
3) Predictability of latency and throughput at peak.
4) Supportability / runbooks for their SRE and change management.
5) Exit/migration plan.

Suggested field scripts (short)
- For compliance officer: "We can show the exact audit trail of any model change, who triggered it, and the signed config snapshot used in production — that is what auditors want to prove."
- For infra lead: "We provide a certified deployment package for your environment, bootstrap scripts, and step-by-step runbook. We also offer an on-prem agent that eliminates egress for sensitive artifacts."
- For procurement: "Commercial terms include a pilot price, a clearly defined deliverable checklist, and an exit data package so you get everything you need to operate independently after the pilot."

Evidence artifacts we've standardized (so far)
- Signed rollout snapshot (JSON) with model version, quantization profile, and policies.
- Audit export that maps request IDs -> policy decisions -> token billing.
- Onboarding runbook and escalation matrix.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Need a short template for the "evidence bundle" that can be shipped post-pilot. OWNER: Samuel.
- Legal: finalize wording for KMS vs HSM obligations in enterprise contract. OWNER: Clara.
- Ops: can we produce a compact signed log format compatible with Splunk/QRadar? OWNER: Jon.

Suggested deliverables for next week
- 1-pager "Evidence bundle checklist" targeted at auditors.
- 3-slide buyer deck for security teams (problem, control plane architecture, evidence examples).
- Two short email templates for AE outreach: compliance-first intro and technical-ops intro.

Sample AE outreach subject lines
- "Quick: how do you prove ML changes to auditors?"
- "Redwood Private — KMS-first control plane for regulated models"

Appendix: rapid objection cheat (one-liners)
- "We can host control endpoints in your VPC": gives reassurance.
- "Telemetry is opt-in and can be sanitized": addresses data leakage fears.
- "You keep the keys and the signed audit trail": addresses encryption/forensics.
- "Exportable artifacts and migration plan included": addresses lock-in.

Version notes
- 0.1 initial draft; field-tested in two pilot conversations (healthtech and payments) — feedback incorporated.

Unpolished / raw notes (keep here for context)
- Healthtech pilot asked for sample SOC2 narratives and for a proof that model changes are observable in SIEM. They wanted a demo where a model rollback appears as an event in Splunk.
- Payments pilot cared about per-token billing tieouts to transaction IDs. They wanted a signed bill-of-requests for a sample day.

If you use/modify this doc:
- Add concrete examples from pilots under a new section "pilot artifacts" and tag the buyer (use initials only).
- Ping me on Slack if you need a 10-min prep before a call.

End of doc.
